odia: ଛେଛରି ଛତା, ହାଟ୍କେ ନେଲେ ପଇସା ହେତା
title: Even the torn umbrella
literal_meaning: A torn umbrella: taken to market, it could have brought money.
explanation: The dictionary spells out the small possibility: the torn umbrella could be sold for money if taken to market. Damage has not automatically made it valueless. The conditional ending makes the value depend on taking it to market; it could sound practical or rueful, depending on the occasion. Our present-day reading asks whether something dismissed as useless still has an honest use or exchange value. It is not a guarantee that every broken object will sell, and the defect should not be hidden from a buyer.
meaning_odia: ଛତାଟି ଚିରା, ତଥାପି ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିଲେ ପଇସା ମିଳନ୍ତା ବୋଲି ଅଭିଧାନ ବୁଝାଇଛି। ଖରାପ ହୋଇଗଲା ମାତ୍ରେ ଜିନିଷଟିର ସବୁ ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଶେଷ ହୋଇନାହିଁ। “ହେତା”ରେ ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିବାର ସର୍ତ୍ତ ସହ ପଇସା ମିଳିବାର ସମ୍ଭାବନା ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଫିଙ୍ଗିଦେବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜିନିଷର ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ କାମକୁ ଭାବିବାର ଅବକାଶ ଅଛି।
english_summary: The damaged object may still bring money if taken to market.
odia_summary: ଚିରା ଜିନିଷ ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ପଇସା ମିଳିପାରେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: During a clear-out, someone is about to discard an old umbrella whose frame can still be used. A friend quotes the line and suggests offering it openly as a damaged item to someone who repairs umbrellas.
cultural_context: The dictionary labels this a Sambalpur form and gives the selling gloss. No standardisation of ହାଟ୍କେ or ହେତା, no market-price claim or fraudulent-sale advice. Practical application is editorial.
